severity_note: Draft educational labels; severity is context dependent. SWC is historical and not a complete current taxonomy.

entries.name: Reentrancy
entries.description: External calls can reenter before state is finalized.
entries.root_cause: State updates after untrusted calls allow repeated execution.

entries.name: Integer overflow and underflow
entries.description: Unchecked arithmetic can wrap numeric values.
entries.root_cause: Arithmetic bounds are not enforced; older Solidity versions require particular care.

entries.name: Unchecked call return value
entries.description: A failed low-level call can be silently ignored.
entries.root_cause: The caller does not inspect the returned success flag.

entries.name: Unprotected Ether withdrawal
entries.description: Unauthorized callers can withdraw contract Ether.
entries.root_cause: Withdrawal functions lack effective caller authorization.

entries.name: Unprotected selfdestruct
entries.description: An exposed destructive operation can disrupt a contract.
entries.root_cause: Sensitive selfdestruct execution lacks authorization; effects depend on chain semantics.

entries.name: Delegatecall to untrusted callee
entries.description: Untrusted delegated code executes in caller storage context.
entries.root_cause: The delegated target is attacker controlled or inadequately constrained.

entries.name: Authorization through tx.origin
entries.description: tx.origin authorization can be bypassed through a malicious intermediary.
entries.root_cause: The original transaction sender is treated as the authorized immediate caller.

entries.name: Transaction order dependence
entries.description: Transaction ordering can change sensitive outcomes.
entries.root_cause: Shared state transitions rely on ordering that block producers can influence.

entries.name: Block values as time proxy
entries.description: Block timing assumptions can make sensitive logic unreliable.
entries.root_cause: Contract logic treats adjustable or approximate block values as precise time.

entries.name: Weak randomness
entries.description: Predictable blockchain values can undermine random selection.
entries.root_cause: Public or influenceable values are used as secret unbiased entropy.

entries.name: Denial of service with failed call
entries.description: A failing recipient can block a larger operation.
entries.root_cause: Progress depends on every external transfer or call succeeding.

entries.name: Denial of service with block gas limit
entries.description: Growing work can exceed the block gas limit.
entries.root_cause: Required operations iterate over unbounded state.

entries.name: Write to arbitrary storage location
entries.description: Unexpected storage writes can corrupt sensitive state.
entries.root_cause: Storage index calculations permit writing unintended locations.

entries.name: Incorrect constructor name
entries.description: Legacy constructor naming mistakes can expose initialization publicly.
entries.root_cause: A function intended as a constructor does not match the legacy contract name.

entries.name: Shadowing state variables
entries.description: A shadowed variable can diverge from the state developers intend to use.
entries.root_cause: Local names, or inherited state-variable names in legacy Solidity, obscure which variable is accessed.

entries.name: Missing protection against signature replay
entries.description: A valid signature can authorize unintended repeated actions.
entries.root_cause: Signed messages lack nonces or adequate domain separation.

entries.name: Lack of proper signature verification
entries.description: Improper signature checks can accept unauthorized messages.
entries.root_cause: Verification does not bind the signer and message to the intended operation.

entries.name: Price oracle manipulation
entries.description: Influenced price feeds can distort protocol decisions.
entries.root_cause: The protocol trusts price inputs attackers can move.

entries.name: Flash loan facilitated attacks
entries.description: Borrowed liquidity can amplify a vulnerable operation in one transaction.
entries.root_cause: Protocol assumptions fail when an attacker temporarily controls substantial liquidity.

entries.name: Business logic errors
entries.description: Contract behavior can violate the intended economic rules despite valid execution.
entries.root_cause: Implementation omits or misapplies a required business invariant.
